sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: What makes you sound the way you do?
sentences.zh: 是什么决定了你说话的声音？

sentences.en: Maybe you've been told that you speak like your mom, or that you laugh like your uncle.
sentences.zh: 也许有人跟你说过，你说话像你妈妈，或者笑起来像你叔叔。

sentences.en: Maybe you sometimes slip back into an accent that reveals something about your paSt.
sentences.zh: 也许你有时会不经意间带出某种口音，暴露了你的过去。

sentences.en: Maybe you have a habit of matching the ways that other people speak when you want to make them more comfortable.
sentences.zh: 也许为了让别人感觉更自在，你习惯模仿别人的说话方式。

sentences.en: Maybe you haven't thought about your voice.
sentences.zh: 也许你从未思考过自己的声音。

sentences.en: Or maybe you think about it all the time.
sentences.zh: 或者你无时无刻不在思考它。
声音对我有着致命的吸引力。

sentences.en: The way a person's voice changes over time feels like a simple and overlooked act of magic.
sentences.zh: 一个人的声音随着时间推移而发生的改变，感觉就像是一个简单却被忽视的魔法。

sentences.en: Whether intentionally or subconsciously, our voices are products of our environments as much as they are part of us.
sentences.zh: 无论是刻意还是潜意识使然，我们的声音既是我们环境的产物，也是我们自身的一部分。

sentences.en: Today we're featuring a series that I'm excited to share with you.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要推出一个我很兴奋能与大家分享的系列节目。

sentences.en: It's called Sounds Gay, a show about queer culture, community, and music.
sentences.zh: 它叫“酷儿之声”，一档聚焦酷儿文化、社群与音乐的节目。

sentences.en: This is an episode that they did about voices, about a videotape, and about sisterhood.
sentences.zh: 这是他们制作的一集关于声音、一盘录像带以及姐妹情谊的节目。

sentences.en: And after the episode, Roman is going to join me for a special conversation.
sentences.zh: 节目结束后，罗曼将加入我进行一场特别的对话。

sentences.en: And in the next 30 minutes, you're going to get everything you need to develop a more feminine voice.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的30分钟里，你将获得培养更女性化嗓音所需的一切知识。

sentences.en: There's seven major areas I've found to be real tools.
sentences.zh: 我发现有七个主要领域是真正的实用工具。

sentences.en: And we're going to cover them all in great detail.
sentences.zh: 我们将在接下来的节目中详细探讨所有这些内容。

sentences.en: If you're a trans woman in 2023, and you want to change your voice to sound more traditionally feminine, you have options.
sentences.zh: 如果你是2023年的一名跨性别女性，并且想改变自己的声音，听起来更具传统女性的特质，你有很多选择。

sentences.en: There are apps, YouTube videos, even online voice coaches.
sentences.zh: 现在有各种应用程序、YouTube视频，甚至在线语音教练。

sentences.en: But if you were a trans woman in the 90s and you wanted to change your voice, you'd want to get your hands on a videotape like Melanie Speaks.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是90年代的一名跨性别女性，想要改变自己的声音，你就会渴望弄到一盘像《梅兰妮开讲》这样的录像带。

sentences.en: Over the course of her 45-minute tape, Melanie offers tips, vocal exercises, and plenty of encouragement.
sentences.zh: 在她这盘45分钟的录像带中，梅兰妮提供了各种小贴士、发声练习以及大量的鼓励。

sentences.en: And she points out that there are many ways to sound feminine.
sentences.zh: 她指出，让声音听起来女性化有很多种不同的方式。

sentences.en: Let me give you a couple of examples.
First of all, look at Suzanne Plachette.
sentences.zh: 首先，看看苏珊·普拉切特。

sentences.en: All of them are very feminine women.
sentences.zh: 她们都是非常女性化的女性。

sentences.en: And yet, each one of them has a very deep voice.
sentences.zh: 然而，她们每个人的声音都很低沉。

sentences.en: It's not where you pitch your voice.
It's what you do with it.
I'm Sarah Essikoff, and this is Sounds Gay, a podcast about the intersection of music and queerness.
sentences.zh: 我是莎拉·埃西科夫，这里是“酷儿之声”，一档探讨音乐与酷儿交叉领域的播客。

sentences.en: This week, we're talking about voices.
Not just vocals in a song, but also speaking voices.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是歌曲里的唱腔，还有说话的声音。

sentences.en: The instrument I'm using to tell you this story right now.
sentences.zh: 也就是我此刻用来向你讲述这个故事的乐器。

sentences.en: We get so much information from how people talk.
sentences.zh: 我们能从人们的谈话中获取大量的信息。

sentences.en: We hear regional accents or slang, the rise and fall of emotion, the scratchiness of a night smoking in the back of a dive bar.
sentences.zh: 我们能听出地方口音或俚语、情绪的起伏、以及在小酒馆后屋通宵抽烟后嗓音的沙哑。

sentences.en: But a trans person's voice might lead to unwanted exposure, even in the most mundane interactions.
sentences.zh: 但跨性别者的声音可能会导致不必要的曝光，即使在最日常的互动中也是如此。

sentences.en: Buying a pack of gum can become a record scratch moment, where suddenly everyone's staring at you.
sentences.zh: 买包口香糖都可能变成一个唱片卡壳般的尴尬瞬间，突然之间所有人都盯着你看。

sentences.en: Your voice can make you stand out when you desperately want to blend in.
sentences.zh: 当你极力想要融入人群时，你的声音却会让你显得格外显眼。

sentences.en: For decades, trans people, especially trans women, whose voices don't change when they take hormone therapy,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，跨性别者，尤其是那些在接受激素治疗后声音不会改变的跨性别女性，

sentences.en: have been teaching each other how to find their new voices.
sentences.zh: 一直在互相传授如何寻找新声音的方法。

sentences.en: And in the 90s, one of the people doing the teaching was a woman named Melanie.
sentences.zh: 在90年代，其中一位传授者是一位名叫梅兰妮的女性。

sentences.en: Today we're asking, how did Melanie help a generation of trans women find their voices?
sentences.zh: 今天我们要探讨的问题是：梅兰妮是如何帮助整整一代跨性别女性找到她们的声音的？

sentences.en: I learned about Melanie Speaks from Sounds Gay Consulting producer and creature of habit, Cass Adair.
sentences.zh: 我是从“酷儿之声”的咨询制作人兼习惯动物卡斯·阿代尔那里了解到《梅兰妮开讲》的。

sentences.en: Chicken and sweet potatoes, which is the only food that I eat.
sentences.zh: 鸡肉和红薯，这也是我吃的唯二食物。

sentences.en: Cass is a media studies professor and is currently writing a book about transgender history and digital media.
sentences.zh: 卡斯是一位媒体研究教授，目前正在写一本关于跨性别历史和数字媒体的书。

sentences.en: So he spends a lot of time in trans archives.
sentences.zh: 因此他花了很多时间泡在跨性别档案馆里。

sentences.en: A lot of what being in an archive is, is just reading old newsletters and old magazines and kind of getting a sense of, like, who the characters are.
sentences.zh: 身处档案馆很大一部分的工作，其实就是阅读旧的时事通讯和旧杂志，然后大致摸清这些人物都是谁。

sentences.en: Melanie advertised her tape in these newsletters.
sentences.zh: 梅兰妮就在这些时事通讯中为她的录像带做过广告。

sentences.en: So she was one of the main characters on Cass's radar.
sentences.zh: 所以她是卡斯雷达上的主要人物之一。

sentences.en: And weirdly, she kept coming up.
sentences.zh: 而且说也奇怪，她总是不断被提起。

sentences.en: Like, I would read, like, a biography of someone who came out in the early 2000s, and then they would mention the same person.
sentences.zh: 比如，当我读到某个在2000年代初出柜的人的传记时，他们就会提到同一个人。

sentences.en: So it was like, oh, weird.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的感觉就是，哇，真奇妙。

sentences.en: Like, clearly she was, like, a big deal.
sentences.zh: 很显然，她曾经是个相当了不起的大人物。

sentences.en: But unlike the other main characters in Cass's research, he'd never actually spoken to Melanie.
sentences.zh: 但与卡斯研究中的其他主要人物不同，他从未真正与梅兰妮交谈过。

sentences.en: He said a lot of the older trans women from that world he would see at conferences or they'd be active on Facebook groups he was in for his research.
sentences.zh: 他说，那个圈子里很多年长的跨性别女性，他要么在会议上见过，要么在为研究而加入的Facebook群组里看她们很活跃。

sentences.en: She just seems like somebody who dropped in, was, like, so important for, like, eight years.
sentences.zh: 她看起来就像那种突然出现，并且在短短大约八年里显得极其重要的人。

sentences.en: And I didn't know where she went.
sentences.zh: 而我却不知道她后来去了哪里。

sentences.en: We wanted to track down Melanie and talk to people who had used her tape.
sentences.zh: 我们想要追踪到梅兰妮，并采访那些使用过她录像带的人。

sentences.en: But first we had to find the tape itself.
sentences.zh: 但首先我们得找到那盘录像带本身。

sentences.en: Cass had never actually seen it.
sentences.zh: 卡斯其实从来没看过它。

sentences.en: But he figured it wouldn't be a problem.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得这应该不成问题。

sentences.en: After all, there's a huge trans archive on the internet where people have scanned zines and newsletters and even, like, random people's scrapbooks.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，互联网上有一个庞大的跨性别档案馆，人们在那里扫描了各种小册子、时事通讯，甚至还有各种随机人群的剪贴簿。

sentences.en: But when Cass went searching for Melanie Speaks, this video that's advertised in all these newsletters, it was nowhere to be found.
sentences.zh: 但当卡斯去搜索《梅兰妮开讲》这部在所有这些时事通讯中做过广告的视频时，却根本无迹可寻。

sentences.en: And the closest I could find was this, like, old website that was basically, like, an advertisement for the video.
sentences.zh: 我能找到最接近的东西，是一个基本上类似于该视频广告的旧网站。

sentences.en: And the website was, like, huge, like, angel fire, GeoCities energy.
sentences.zh: 那个网站给人的感觉非常有年代感，充满了火星网（Angelfire）和地沟网（GeoCities）的气息。

sentences.en: Next, Cass searched the largest library catalog in the world and found exactly one copy of Melanie Speaks.
sentences.zh: 接着，卡斯搜索了世界上最大的图书馆目录，结果只找到了唯一的一份《梅兰妮开讲》复制品。

sentences.en: It was at a library in Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 它保存在康涅狄格州的一家图书馆里。

sentences.en: Once we had the tape, we wanted to talk to women who actually used Melanie Speaks back in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们拿到了录像带，我们就想采访那些在90年代真正使用过《梅兰妮开讲》的女性。

sentences.en: One of these women was Gwen Smith.
sentences.zh: 其中一位女性是格温·史密斯。

sentences.en: At the time, Gwen was, like any cool 90s chick, listening to a lot of women singer-songwriters and practicing singing along.
sentences.zh: 当时，格温和任何酷炫的90年代女孩一样，听了大量女性创作歌手的歌，并练习跟着一起唱。

sentences.en: Jagged Little Till and Alanis Morissette was in the playliSt.
sentences.zh: 阿兰妮斯·莫里塞特的《碎裂》也在播放列表中。

sentences.en: I also tended to listen to a lot of Melissa Etheridge's Brave and Crazy and Katie Lang.
sentences.zh: 我也倾向于听很多梅莉莎·埃瑟里奇的《勇敢与疯狂》以及k.d. lang的歌。
天哪，简直一直在听k.d. lang。

sentences.en: It's just, I still adore that album today.
sentences.zh: 至今我依然深爱着那张专辑。

sentences.en: Gwen read about Melanie Speaks in an online chat room.
sentences.zh: 格温是在一个在线聊天室里了解到《梅兰妮开讲》的。

sentences.en: But remember, this was the 1990s internet.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，这是1990年代的互联网。

sentences.en: The chat rooms were text only.
sentences.zh: 当时的聊天室只有纯文本。

sentences.en: You couldn't just upload a video.
sentences.zh: 你可没法直接上传视频。

sentences.en: So Gwen sent for her copy of Melanie Speaks via snail mail.
sentences.zh: 所以格温是通过传统邮件寄信购买了她的《梅兰妮开讲》复制品。

sentences.en: If you want to order a copy of this tape, send $20.
sentences.zh: 如果你想订购这盘录像带的复制品，请寄20美元。

sentences.en: VHS only is available at this time.
sentences.zh: 目前仅提供VHS录像带格式。

sentences.en: Up until that point, any knowledge I had about things trans was people that were in a book or were in a newspaper headline.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，我对跨性别事务的所有了解，都来自于书本上或报纸头条里的那些人。

sentences.en: And a lot of these individuals were fairly wealthy or well-off in their own ways or at least projected that.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人以各自的方式相当富有或优渥，至少呈现出来的形象是这样的。

sentences.en: And me being, at that point, a fairly young person who is working just a 9 to 5, feeling like, well, can I even do this from where I am in this world?
sentences.zh: 而当时的我还算是个年轻人，只做着朝九晚五的工作，心里难免犯嘀咕：就凭我现在的处境，我真的能做到这一点吗？

sentences.en: In her tape, Melanie offered an emphatic, yes, you can do this, to women like Gwen.
sentences.zh: 在她的录像带中，梅兰妮向格温这样的女性给予了坚定而有力的肯定：是的，你能做到。

sentences.en: I could be everything I always wanted to be just by learning this little routine.
sentences.zh: 只要学会这套小小的日常练习，我就能成为我一直想成为的一切。

sentences.en: Once you've found it, it may take you two weeks to find it.
sentences.zh: 一旦你找到了它，可能需要两周时间来寻找。

sentences.en: It may take you a month to find it.
sentences.zh: 也可能需要一个月来寻找。

sentences.en: But believe me, listen to me.
I think Melanie's tape, one way or another, has become the basis for a lot of other people talking about voice.
sentences.zh: 我认为梅兰妮的录像带，无论以何种方式，都已经成为许多其他人探讨声音的基础。

sentences.en: I know that I've taught people some of the things that I learned off those tapes to try to help them with their voice.
sentences.zh: 我知道我已经把从那些录像带中学到的一些东西教给了别人，以此来帮助他们改善声音。

sentences.en: I'm sure there are any number of other people that have just passed on some of that knowledge over time.
sentences.zh: 我确信还有许许多多其他人，随着时间的推移，也传承了其中一部分知识。

sentences.en: Thousands of miles away from Gwen, another woman named Dallas Denny was using the tape, too.
sentences.zh: 在距离格温数千英里之外，另一位名叫达拉斯·登妮的女性也在使用这盘录像带。

sentences.en: Dallas lived in Nashville, Tennessee, and started going out in women's clothing in her early teens.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯住在田纳西州纳什维尔，在十几岁刚出头的时候就开始穿着女装出门了。

sentences.en: I would go to the library, to Woolworths, to the department stores, to the movies, out to eat, ride the buses.
sentences.zh: 我会去图书馆、伍尔沃斯百货商店、百货公司、看电影、出去吃饭、坐公交车。

sentences.en: I didn't feel like I was dressed if I didn't have bonsai lashes.
sentences.zh: 如果没戴夸张的假睫毛，我都觉得自己没穿衣服一样。

sentences.en: So I was wondering for years, was I just deceiving myself, or was I really passing?
sentences.zh: 所以我多年来一直在想，我是在自欺欺人，还是真的成功蒙混过关了？

sentences.en: So I would do things like buy a dress in the checkout line at the department store and ask them if they could tell I was really a guy.
sentences.zh: 所以我有时会做一些事情，比如在百货公司的收银台买一条裙子，然后问他们能不能看出我其实是个男的。

sentences.en: Even though Dallas was wearing false eyelashes and buying dresses as a teenager,
sentences.zh: 尽管达拉斯在十几岁时就戴着假睫毛、买着裙子，

sentences.en: she didn't encounter the larger trans community until she was 38.
sentences.zh: 但直到38岁时，她才真正接触到更大的跨性别社群。

sentences.en: That's when she heard about a trans support group in Atlanta,
sentences.zh: 就在那时，她听说亚特兰大有一个跨性别互助小组，

sentences.en: about 250 miles from where she was living at the time in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 距离她当时在田纳西州的住处大约250英里。

sentences.en: Finally, after 25 years of searching for people like her, she found them.
sentences.zh: 最终，在寻找同类25年后，她找到了他们。

sentences.en: And eventually that community led her to Melanie Speaks.
sentences.zh: 而那个社群最终把她引向了《梅兰妮开讲》。

sentences.en: Dallas doesn't remember exactly where she heard about the tape,
sentences.zh: 达拉斯记不清自己具体是在哪里听说这盘录像带的了，

sentences.en: but she figures it was at a support group or a conference.
sentences.zh: 但她估计是在某个互助小组或会议上。

sentences.en: One thing Dallas appreciated about Melanie's approach
sentences.zh: 达拉斯对梅兰妮的方法非常欣赏的一点是，

sentences.en: was that she didn't take herself or her methods too seriously.
sentences.zh: 她并没有把自己或她的方法看得太严肃。

sentences.en: The other way is to go directly into that voice and go kind of like this.
sentences.zh: 另一种方法是直接进入那种声音，然后大致发出这样的声音。

sentences.en: Like you're saying, yeah, I'm a New York City cab driver.
sentences.zh: 就像你在说，嗨，我是纽约市的出租车司机。

sentences.en: And gosh, that's a Midwest accent and then New York City.
sentences.zh: 天哪，那是中西部口音，然后是纽约市口音。

sentences.en: Well, he came from the Midwest originally.
Her silly voices made me realize that if you're going to change things,
sentences.zh: 她那些滑稽的声音让我意识到，如果你想要改变现状，

sentences.en: you have to get out of your zone.
sentences.zh: 你就必须跳出自己的舒适区。

sentences.en: And what better way to do it than to go on all the way out there
sentences.zh: 还有什么比用你声音所能做出的最诡异的事情，

sentences.en: with the most bizarre things you can do with your voice
and then reeling it back in until you find it, you know her.
sentences.zh: 然后把它一点点收回来，直到你找到感觉更好的方法更好的办法呢？

sentences.en: Well, after you do that, you can get down here
sentences.zh: 好吧，当你做完这些后，你可以把音调降到这里

sentences.en: and then you sound like the typical Southern Bale.
sentences.zh: 然后你的声音听起来就像典型的南方淑女。

sentences.en: And you can say, oh, Magnolia, it's just marvelous, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 你可以说，哦，木兰花，这简直太奇妙了，不是吗？

sentences.en: But then you bring it out even a little bit more
sentences.zh: 但随后你再把它稍微往外释放一点

sentences.en: and then you get into the typical American voice,
sentences.zh: 然后你就会进入典型的美国声音，

sentences.en: I really like what she was advocating about,
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢她所倡导的那种理念，

sentences.en: just going through a phase of exploration with your voice,
sentences.zh: 也就是经历一个对声音的探索阶段，

sentences.en: because a lot of the people that I knew were just refusing to do that
sentences.zh: 因为我认识的很多人都拒绝这样做，

sentences.en: because they thought it made them sound silly or gay.
sentences.zh: 因为他们觉得这让他们听起来很滑稽或者很娘。

sentences.en: Dallas thinks this fear of sounding silly or gay
sentences.zh: 达拉斯认为，这种害怕听起来滑稽或娘的恐惧，

sentences.en: held women back from finding their true voices.
sentences.zh: 阻碍了女性寻找自己真正的声音。

sentences.en: But it was also a legitimate fear to have,
sentences.zh: 但这也是一种合情合理的恐惧，

sentences.en: because in the 90s, passing as cisgender was considered imperative.
sentences.zh: 因为在90年代，被当作顺性别看待被认为是至关重要的。

sentences.en: At the time, you were supposed to pass.
sentences.zh: 当时，你理应做到让人看不出破绽。
每个人都渴望不被看出破绽。

sentences.en: No one thought about it being okay not to pass.
